For \( P(x) \) to have a real root, \( \frac{x^{n+1} - 1}{x - 1} = 0 \) must have a real solution. This equation simplifies to \( x^{n+1} - 1 = 0 \) for \( x \neq 1 \), which means \( x^{n+1} = 1 \). The real solutions to this equation are \( x = 1 \) and \( x = -1 \) when \( n+1 \) is even. However, \( x = 1 \) is not a valid solution because it makes the denominator zero in the original expression. Therefore, the only possible real root is \( x = -1 \), which requires \( n+1 \) to be even, i.e., \( n \) must be odd.
